qbcf071c5.question: OWNER DECISION: with no queue in this window (node:sqlite cannot load, or a newer-schema file), should a review-pane decision be refused with a note (this LLD's choice: the decision stays recorded and the pane says the chat could not be told), or keep a direct-run fallback for that case? The HLD removes the waiting list entirely, so a fallback would keep part of what S005 removes. Recommendation: refuse with a note.
qbcf071c5.choice: No fallback anywhere: when the chat queue cannot be opened (node:sqlite cannot load, or the queue file is from a newer plugin) the chat is disabled. extension.ts does not register the chat command and shows the existing unsupported-VS-Code notice once; there is no direct-run path to keep working. A review-pane decision therefore reaches submitExternal only in a window that has a queue; submitExternal still returns unavailable with a note if it is ever called without one, and keeps no waiting list. The host's own internal no-queue branches (sendTyped's direct runTurn) are not rewritten in this Story: removing them rewrites hundreds of host tests and belongs to a separate cleanup.
qbcf071c5.rationale: Owner decision: chat is a core feature; a fallback path is too complicated to keep functional, so without sqlite the chat is disabled.

qcd5a85b2.question: OWNER DECISION: eviction skips every session with live queue rows in any repository, so the 200-session history can grow above its cap while many sessions hold waiting or failed messages. Accept that, or evict a kept session anyway once the history passes a hard ceiling (and fail its message with the chat gone)? Recommendation: accept; rows are bounded at 500 per repository, so the overshoot is bounded too.
qcd5a85b2.choice: The 200-session history cap is a hard cap and eviction is unchanged: the oldest session is evicted even if it still has queue rows, and such a message then fails with 'the chat no longer exists' (S001's existing path) and offers a resend. No keep predicate on the session store and no cross-repository reader of other queue files are added; protecting sessions beyond the cap is over-engineering. The start-up attachment sweep already keeps every session still in the store (chatKeep), so a waiting message's attachments survive it; Story S005 only pins that with a test.
qcd5a85b2.rationale: Owner decision: hard cap of 200; anything more is unrealistic and over-engineering.

q719063a7.question: cd1 (partial): liveSessionIdsOfAllQueues and the keepSessionIds dependency are new names this Story introduces; they are labelled new in dataModel and are not existing symbols.
q719063a7.choice: Moot: the owner's hard-cap ruling removes liveSessionIdsOfAllQueues and the keepSessionIds dependency from the design, so no new names remain to ground. The LLD is amended to drop them.

qbabde9a5.question: ep3 (partial): the invariantsToPreserve cite the HLD assumption ids c3, c11 and c12 as the schema requires; the behaviours are shown by the read:queue-surface and read:current-behaviour bundles, but the ids do not name a bundle directly.
qbabde9a5.choice: Add a bundle crosswalk in the plan: keep the HLD c-ids (c3, c11, c12) in the LLD and map them to the read:queue-surface and read:current-behaviour bundles in the plan's closing task, as ruled for s4.
qbabde9a5.rationale: Same ruling as Story s4 (option A there).

summary.prose: A decision sent from the document review pane now joins the repository's chat queue like a typed message: it waits in the chat's outbox behind any running turn, survives the panel or window closing, and runs in order. The review pane's own in-memory waiting list is removed. Where the chat queue cannot be opened (node:sqlite cannot load, or a newer-schema queue file) the chat is disabled, with no fallback path. The 200-session history cap stays a hard cap.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A shared per-repository SQLite queue (node:sqlite, WAL, busy timeout) under ~/.insrc, written only in short IMMEDIATE transactions, with three tables: messages in queue order, a single-row repo lease with a heartbeat, and window presence keyed by a window key that survives a reload. A deps-injected queue worker in each window decides from the database alone when to take the lease, acknowledges the head message (queued -> processing) in the same transaction, and hands the turn to the existing turn lifecycle with its newest-wins rule removed; the per-session lease stays underneath as a guard against two CLI processes on one session. Takeover, not-delivered marking, retries and the flush are rules over these tables, and the outbox is a projection of them posted to the chat webview.

boundary.internal: A pane decision goes to the chat the review pane hands over to today: the chat shown in this window's panel, or, when the panel is closed, the chat the panel opens on (this window's last active chat). It is submitted through ChatQueueWorker.submit with origin 'review-pane', and the panel is opened. submitExternal returns 'queued' | { kind: 'unavailable'; note }; the review host's notifyChat type, ChatHandOver and decisionResultLine carry the note. The waitingExternal list and drainExternal are removed. Attachments: the live session ids across every repository's queue file are added to the start-up sweep's keep set, and session eviction skips any session with live rows in any queue through a keep dependency on the file session store.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — retries and the review pane

api.name: submitExternal
api.signature: submitExternal(text: string): ExternalSubmitResult  // type ExternalSubmitResult = 'queued' | { readonly kind: 'unavailable'; readonly note: string }

parameters.name: text
parameters.purpose: The decision message the review pane composed.

returns.meaning: 'queued' when the message joined the repository's queue; otherwise { kind: 'unavailable', note } with a sentence saying why (blank text, no agentic CLI installed, or the queue's own refusal: full or busy). A window without a queue has no chat and no notifyChat binding, so submitExternal is not reached there.

errors.condition: every refusal is a returned unavailable result; a throw from the queue is caught and returned as unavailable

preconditions: text is a non-empty string after trimming
this window has a queue worker (without one the chat is not offered and the review pane is given no hand-over)
postconditions: on 'queued' the panel is open, the target chat is saved, and one row with origin 'review-pane' exists in the queue for that chat
no in-memory list holds the message
the running turn and its waiting cards are not touched

api.name: ChatQueueWorker.submit
api.signature: submit(m: { sessionId: string; text: string; origin: 'typed' | 'review-pane'; attachments: readonly AttachmentRef[] }): EnqueueResult

parameters.name: m
parameters.purpose: The message to queue, here with origin 'review-pane' and no attachments.

returns.meaning: ok with the stored row, or a refusal reason (full, busy, unavailable) with a note.

errors.condition: the queue is at QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND, busy, or unavailable

preconditions: the chat session is saved so it exists when the message runs
postconditions: the row is visible in every window's outbox for that chat

api.name: notifyChat
api.signature: notifyChat?: (text: string) => ExternalSubmitResult   // the review host's dependency, was 'sent' | 'queued' | 'unavailable'

returns.meaning: The hand-over outcome, with the refusal note carried for the pane.

errors.condition: the host's handOver catches it and reports 'failed'; the decision stays recorded

postconditions: the decision is already recorded before the hand-over is attempted

api.name: decisionResultLine
api.signature: decisionResultLine(res: ReviewDecisionResult, sent: number, chat: ChatHandOver): string   // type ChatHandOver = 'queued' | { kind: 'unavailable'; note: string } | 'failed' | 'none'

returns.meaning: The one line the pane shows: 'queued' reads 'Sent to the chat; it waits its turn in the outbox.'; unavailable reads 'The chat could not be told: <note>'; failed and none are unchanged; the 'sent' wording is gone.

postconditions: a refused decision names why it was refused

dataModelChanges.details: 'sent' is removed; unavailable becomes an object carrying the note so the pane can say why.
The in-memory list, its drain at about ten call sites, and its drop-with-warning on panel or host close are removed; dropExternal's reset of webviewReady stays under a clearer name.

When createQueueFactory returns undefined (node:sqlite cannot load, or a newer-schema queue file) the chat is not offered in that window, with no direct-run path. In extension.ts, everything that turns the chat on is gated on the queue existing: (1) the insrc.chat.open command is not registered, and package.json gains a menus.commandPalette entry for it with when: insrc.chat.ready, so the Command Palette does not list a command that is not there; (2) setContext('insrc.chat.ready', true), which shows the editor-title chat icon, is not called; (3) the WebviewPanelSerializer for the chat view type is not registered, so a chat tab restored after a reload is not wired to the host (the restored tab is left empty and closes); (4) the review host is given no notifyChat binding, so the review pane still works for its own decisions and shows 'No chat message was sent.'. ANY failure to open the queue disables the chat, since createQueueFactory catches every error from opening the store (a failed mkdir, a permission error, a corrupt or locked file, as well as the two named causes). Three notices, chosen by cause: a StoreUnavailable matching /newer plugin/ -> 'The chat is disabled in this window: its queue was made by a newer insrc plugin; reload this window.'; an error that is the failure to load node:sqlite (ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE, or a message naming node:sqlite) -> 'The chat is disabled in this window: this VS Code cannot load node:sqlite, which the chat queue needs.'; any other failure -> 'The chat is disabled in this window: its queue could not be opened (<the error's message>).'. The module doc comments that say the chat 'stays on its direct path' (chat-queue-setup.ts header, extension.ts near the queue factory) are updated. The host's internal no-queue branches stay and are not reachable from the extension; removing them is a separate cleanup.
callSites: vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts (insrc.chat.open registration, setContext insrc.chat.ready, registerWebviewPanelSerializer, the review host's notifyChat binding)
vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-queue-setup.ts (the two notices and the header comment)

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Unchanged. This Story reads and writes the queue only through the worker's submit; it adds no reader of the queue files.
submitExternal calls ChatQueueWorker.submit with origin 'review-pane'. worker.liveSessionIds() is not consumed: the sweep and eviction rules are unchanged.
A review-pane row reaches the outbox through the existing projection, which already carries origin 'review-pane'; no change to OutboxView or its actions.

errorCases.scenario: The chat queue cannot be created in this window (node:sqlite cannot load, a newer-schema queue file, or any other failure to open the store)
errorCases.detection: createQueueFactory returns undefined at start-up: it catches every error from opening the store
errorCases.response: The chat is disabled in this window: the chat command, the chat icon's ready context and the chat tab serializer are not registered, and the review host gets no notifyChat binding; the notice says the chat is disabled and names the cause (sqlite cannot load, newer plugin, or the open error's message)
errorCases.userImpact: No chat in that window. A review-pane decision is still recorded and the pane says 'No chat message was sent.'

errorCases.scenario: The queue refuses the message: at QUEUE_RECORD_BOUND, or busy
errorCases.detection: ChatQueueWorker.submit returns { ok: false, reason, note }
errorCases.response: Return unavailable with the queue's own note
errorCases.userImpact: The pane shows 'The chat could not be told: <note>'; nothing is queued

errorCases.scenario: No agentic CLI is installed, or the text is blank or not a string
errorCases.detection: deps.providers.available.length === 0, or typeof text !== 'string' or text.trim() === ''
errorCases.response: Return unavailable with a note for that cause, before any panel is opened or session saved
errorCases.userImpact: The pane says why the chat could not be told

errorCases.scenario: The target chat session is gone when the message reaches the front (evicted at the hard 200-session cap, or removed)
errorCases.detection: queueRunner.run finds deps.store.get(sessionId) undefined and resolves failed 'the chat no longer exists' (S001)
errorCases.response: Unchanged: the row ends failed with a resend. Eviction does not protect sessions with live rows (the cap is hard)
errorCases.userImpact: The outbox shows the failed decision with resend and dismiss; the message text is kept so it can be resent into another chat

errorCases.scenario: Saving the draft chat fails before the message is queued
errorCases.detection: Not detected at submit: trySave (via trySaveSession) only logs a failed save and returns nothing; the failure is seen later when the runner finds no session and resolves failed 'the chat no longer exists'
errorCases.response: Proceed as typed messages do: the submit still happens. If the unsaved draft is still the shown chat in the window that runs the message, it runs against the in-memory draft and succeeds. The runner fails the message with 'the chat no longer exists' only when the message is run by another window, or after the chat was switched or the window reloaded (it reads the store only when the shown session is a different chat)
errorCases.userImpact: Rare; the decision may show as failed with a resend

edgeCases.expected: It queues behind that message in strict order; this chat's outbox shows it with the count of other chats' messages ahead

edgeCases.input: A decision is sent while the shown chat has a waiting approval card
edgeCases.expected: It waits in the outbox behind the running turn and the card; submitting never answers or rejects the card

edgeCases.input: The panel is closed and no chat was ever shown in this window
edgeCases.expected: The panel opens on a draft chat, the draft is saved, and the decision is queued for that chat

edgeCases.input: The panel is closed after a chat was shown earlier in this window
edgeCases.expected: The decision goes to that last shown chat, the panel opens on it

edgeCases.input: Two decisions are sent back to back
edgeCases.expected: Two rows in the outbox, in send order; each runs in turn

edgeCases.input: The window is reloaded after the decision is queued and before it runs
edgeCases.expected: The row is in the file, so it survives; the reloaded window's worker runs it when it reaches the front, opening the panel

edgeCases.input: A session with a waiting message and attachments is in the store at start-up
edgeCases.expected: The sweep's keep set already holds every stored session, so its attachments are kept and go with the message when it runs

edgeCases.input: More than 200 sessions exist and the oldest has a waiting message
edgeCases.expected: It is evicted by the hard cap; its message fails with 'the chat no longer exists' and can be resent

invariantsToPreserve.text: Submitting a message never touches the running turn, its waiting cards or the approval grant chain; a pane decision, like a typed one, waits its turn.
A decision is recorded by the review host before the chat is told, and a failed hand-over never undoes it.
Queue order is strict per repository: a review-pane message is an ordinary row and runs at its place in seq order.
Only the worker writes the queue, in short IMMEDIATE transactions; this Story adds no other reader or writer of the queue files.

migration.stateBefore: A pane decision goes through submitExternal into the chat host's in-memory waitingExternal list and is run by drainExternal directly through runTurn when this window is idle (bundle read:current-behaviour). It bypasses the repository queue, so another window's running message does not hold it, and it is dropped when the panel or the window closes. A window without a queue runs the chat on a direct path.
migration.stateAfter: A pane decision is submitted through the repository's queue worker with origin 'review-pane' and is an ordinary row: it waits in the chat's outbox, survives the panel or window closing, and runs in order. The waiting list and its drain are gone. A window that cannot open the queue has the chat disabled.

migrationSteps.action: Change submitExternal to submit through the worker and return the new result; change the review host's notifyChat type, ChatHandOver and decisionResultLine to carry the note; update the binding
Remove waitingExternal, drainExternal and its call sites; keep the webviewReady reset that dropExternal performs

In extension.ts, when the queue cannot be created: do not register insrc.chat.open, do not set insrc.chat.ready, do not register the chat tab serializer and do not pass notifyChat to the review host; reword the notices in chat-queue-setup.ts to say the chat is disabled and add a third for any other open failure, and update the comments that say it stays on a direct path; add the menus.commandPalette entry for insrc.chat.open in package.json

Rewrite or remove the tests that pinned 'sent', the old wording, the drain order, the direct path and the old notices (chat-panel.test.ts submitExternal suite, docs-review-decision.test.ts, review-wiring.test.ts, chat-queue-setup.test.ts); add the queue-path tests, the extension wiring tests and the sweep test

migration.backwardCompat: No stored data changes: the queue file's schema, the session files and the attachment directories are untouched. The review host's notifyChat dependency changes its return type, internal to the plugin and changed in one commit with its only binding. Behaviour change: a VS Code that cannot load node:sqlite no longer runs the chat on a direct path; the chat is not offered there (owner decision). Mixed plugin versions: a window still running the previous plugin starts a pane decision directly outside the queue until it is reloaded, as typed messages already do (S001).

alternativesConsidered.name: Submit through the worker; hard 200-session cap, sweep unchanged
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: submitExternal submits through ChatQueueWorker; the sweep's existing keep set already holds every stored session; no new reader and no keep predicate.
alternativesConsidered.approach: submitExternal drops the waiting list: it resolves the target chat (the shown session, or after opening the panel the session it opens on), saves a draft so the chat exists, submits with origin 'review-pane' and returns 'queued' or { kind: 'unavailable', note }. A window without a queue does not offer the chat. The start-up sweep's keep set (chatKeep, every session in the store) already protects a waiting message's attachments; the 200-session cap stays hard, so an evicted session's message fails with the chat gone and a resend.
pros: No new reader of queue files and no change to the session store
No change to the queue store, the worker contract or the schema
Smallest change that removes the waiting list
cons: A session evicted at the hard cap loses its waiting message (it fails with the chat gone and can be resent)

alternativesConsidered.name: Submit through the worker; use only this window's worker.liveSessionIds()
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep only what the open repository's worker already reports.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same submitExternal change as a1, but the keep set is worker.liveSessionIds() of this window's own repository queue, passed to the sweep and to the store's keep predicate. Other repositories' queue files are not read.
pros: Uses the existing liveSessionIds, no new reader
No file listing or extra database opens
cons: A session with live rows in another repository's queue is still swept or evicted by this window, after which that message fails with the chat gone and its attachments are deleted: the acceptance criterion fails across repositories
The worker exists only after the chat host is built, later than the store and the start-up sweep, so the keep set would need late wiring
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: ac3 is only partly met: it protects only the open repository's sessions, and the worker does not exist when the start-up sweep runs.

alternativesConsidered.name: Submit through the worker; record the kept sessions in a shared index file
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every window writes the session ids of its live rows to a small index and the sweep and eviction read that.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same submitExternal change as a1. Each worker writes ~/.insrc/chat-queue/live-sessions.json (or per-repository files) whenever its rows change, and the sweep and eviction read the union of the index files.
pros: Reading is a few small files, no SQLite open
Would work even if node:sqlite could not load in the reading process
cons: A second copy of queue state that must be kept in step on every commit and every crash, with its own staleness
New writes on every change in every window, and a stale index after a crash can protect nothing or the wrong sessions
Adds a write path to S001's worker, which this Story does not own
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: It partly meets ac3 (a stale index after a crash) and sc4 (it adds a write path in s1's worker), and duplicates queue state.
